sentences.text: 1  BEFORE  HONOURABLE MRS. JUSTICE SHAMIMA JAHAN  ORDER 03.02.2026 Heard Mr. S.C. Biswas, learned counsel for the petitioner.

Also heard Mr. M.P.
Goswami, learned Addl. Public Prosecutor for the State and Ms. P. Das, learned Amicus Curiae for respondent Nos. 2 & 3.
2.

By this application filed under Section 528 of BNSS, 2023, the petitioner has prayed for quashing of the FIR, Charge-sheet and the subsequent proceeding initiated in Session Special Case No.
45/2025 registered under Section 376 IPC read with Section 4 of the POCSO Act pending in the Court of Additional Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Kamrup (M), Guwahati.

entities.text: Court of Additional Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Kamrup (M), Guwahati
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The petitioner has also challenged the Order dated 12.03.2024 passed by the learned Additional CJM,
Karimganj in CR Case No. 280/2024, by which the learned Court had invoked the provision of Section 156(3) Cr.PC for registration of the case by the O/C Nilambazar.

3. Mr. S.C. Biswas, learned counsel for the petitioner has raised the preliminary issue of directing the Police to investigate under Section 156(3) Cr.PC by the Court of Additional CJM, Karimganj at Karimganj.

entities.text: Court of Additional CJM, Karimganj at Karimganj
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He submits that there is total violation of the law laid down by the Apex Court, inasmuch as, it is clearly held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Priyanka Srivastava and Another Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Others reported in (2015) 6 SCC 287 that before filing a petition under Section 156(3) Cr.PC, the complainant is required to take recourse to remedies available under Sections 154(1) and 154(3) of the Cr.PC.

entities.text: Priyanka Srivastava and Another Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Others reported in (2015) 6 SCC 287
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also held that in the application filed under Page No.# 3/4 Section 156(3) Cr.PC, both the aspects that the complainant has approach the O/C of the respective Police Station under Sections 154(1) and 154(3) Cr.PC and that no relief was granted to the complainant.
It is also held that the said application under Section 156(3) Cr.PC should be accompanied by an affidavit.

4. Mr. S.C. Biswas, learned counsel for the petitioner points out that in the instant complaint, no such averment is made by the complainant that they had approached the concerned authority under Section 154(1) and 154(3) of the Cr.PC and as such, he submits that the said direction by the Court of Additional CJM, Karimganj is not in accordance with law.
5. Mr. M.P. Goswami, learned Addl.
Public Prosecutor for the State submits that under Section 156(3) Cr.PC, the Magistrate has ample power to direct investigation by the Police in respect of the complaint filed by the complainant.
He further submits that the TCR has been called for and necessary orders may be passed after perusal of the same.

6. Ms. P. He also submits that the TCR may be looked into and necessary orders may be passed.
7.
I have heard the learned counsels for the parties.

8. It is no res-integra that the Apex Court has time and again held that the complainant before making an application under Section 156(3) of Cr.PC to the Magistrate should approach the Police under Section 154(1) and if the Police refuse to register the case, the complainant has power to complaint before the Page No.# 4/4 Superintendant of Police as required under the law.
It is also held by the Supreme Court that the said recourse that the complainant has taken should be averred in the complaint petition, where Section 156(3) Cr.PC prayer is made.
9. In the instant case, it is seen that no such averment is made in the complaint petition that the complainant has approached the Police for necessary relief.
A further requirement is also laid by the Supreme Court that the complaint petition, where prayer for Police investigation is made should be accompanied by an affidavit.
However, the same is done in the instant case but the necessary averment is absent.

Further, it is also seen that the learned Additional CJM, Karimganj prima facie has not applied its mind before sending the case for investigation to the O/C Nilambazar Police Station, which is required under the law and as held by the Apex Court.
As such, this Court finds it fit that the proceedings initiated in the Session Special Case No. 45/2025 may be stayed until the next returnable date.
10. TCR has already been called for and a reminder was also issued but the same has not been received.

As such, Registry may send a reminder again or get a report from the Court of Additional Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Kamrup (M), Guwahati as to why the TCR has not been sent to this Court.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 11. List this matter again on 23.02.2026.
